title: Smooth manifolds
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Learn the language of modern geometry: smooth manifolds and smooth maps, partitions of unity, tangent spaces and differentials, submersions, immersions and embeddings, submanifolds and the regular value theorem, Sard's theorem in outline, vector fields, flows and Lie brackets, Lie groups, vector bundles and differential forms, the exterior derivative, orientation and integration, Stokes's theorem, de Rham cohomology, and Riemannian metrics.
primary_reading: Lecture notes on smooth manifolds by Marco Gualtieri, University of Toronto (free PDF)

weeks.1: Topological and smooth manifolds, charts and atlases
weeks.2: Smooth maps and partitions of unity
weeks.5: Submanifolds and the regular value theorem
weeks.6: Sard's theorem and transversality in outline
weeks.7: Vector fields, integral curves and flows
weeks.9: Vector bundles, covectors and differential forms
weeks.10: The exterior derivative, orientation and integration
weeks.12: De Rham cohomology and Riemannian metrics

blocks.deliverable: Show that spheres and projective spaces are smooth manifolds.
Compute differentials and decide which supplied maps are immersions.
Prove that a supplied level set is a submanifold.
Week 7 midterm; compute the flows and Lie brackets of supplied vector fields.
Integrate a supplied differential form over an oriented manifold.
Compute the de Rham cohomology of the circle and the punctured plane.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in geometry: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems on manifolds, forms and Stokes's theorem, prove the regular value theorem and Stokes's theorem in full, check Stokes's theorem numerically in plain Python on two examples, and write a two-page guide to the definitions and theorems with their hypotheses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
